VIOLENCE
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

So we as a society or as law enforcement officials need to give women the opportunity to express their interests regarding everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of the violence that befalls them.

Article 4
The purpose of establishing this Regional Regulation is to provide protection and services to women and children who are victims of gender-based violence, based on the best interests of the child, occurring in the household and/or in public spaces, as well as to guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination, for the realization of Indonesian children who are of quality, of noble character, and prosperous.

Article 4O
Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 30 includes: physical, psychological, and sexual violence carried out through efforts: dissemination and socialization of statutory provisions that protect child victims of criminal acts of violence; and monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.
Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, (2) ordering to commit, or participating in committing violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as regulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and the entire territory of Indonesia, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on: (a) independence, (b) eternal peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the teachings of trias politica, there are three State powers namely executive power for the administration of government, legislative power as the formulator of laws and regulations and judicial power as the implementer of laws and regulations. In Indonesia, these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of clean and authoritative government, from the national level to the regional level.
The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of Power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.
The Rights of Women and Children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.
Regional Autonomy that is implemented, has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (Regional Regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to become a guideline for Regional Governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

Protection of children, not only those who are victims of violence, but also those undergoing judicial processes, as regulated in Law Number 11 of 2012 concerning the Juvenile Justice System, as an improvement to Law Number 3 of 1997 concerning Juvenile Courts, which in Article 3 stipulates that: Every Child in the criminal justice process has the right to:
a. be treated humanely with attention to needs according to their age; b. be separated from adults; c. obtain legal assistance and other assistance effectively; d. engage in recreational activities; e. be free from torture, punishment or other treatment that is cruel, inhumane, and degrading to their dignity and honor; f. not be sentenced to death or life imprisonment; g. not be arrested, detained, or imprisoned, except as a last resort and for the shortest time; h. obtain justice before a Juvenile Court that is objective, impartial, and in a closed session to the public; i. not have their identity published; j. obtain accompaniment from parents/Guardians and persons trusted by the Child; k. obtain social advocacy; l. obtain private life; m. obtain accessibility, especially for disabled children; n. obtain education; From the provisions of the legislation above, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when becoming victims of violence, but in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as regulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and the entire territory of Indonesia, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on: (a) independence, (b) eternal peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the teachings of trias politica, there are three State powers namely executive power for the administration of government, legislative power as the formulator of laws and regulations and judicial power as the implementer of laws and regulations. In Indonesia, these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of clean and authoritative government, from the national level to the regional level.
The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of Power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.
The Rights of Women and Children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.
Regional Autonomy that is implemented, has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (Regional Regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to become a guideline for Regional Governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as regulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and the entire territory of Indonesia, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on: (a) independence, (b) eternal peace, and (c) social justice. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. Article 57
The judge on their own initiative or upon request of the parties, public prosecutor, legal counsel and/or victim may order a Woman in Contact with the Law to have her testimony heard through examination via remote audio visual communication at the local court or at another location, if:
1) The mental/psychological condition of the Woman in Contact with the Law is unhealthy due to fear/psychological trauma based on the assessment of a doctor or psychologist;
2) Based on the judge's assessment, the safety of the Woman in Contact with the Law cannot be guaranteed if she is in a public and open place; or
3) Based on the decision of the Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK), the Woman in Contact with the Law is declared to be in a witness and/or victim protection program and, according to LPSK, cannot attend the trial to give testimony either due to security reasons or due to obstacles, or due to physical and psychological obstacles.

Article 56
If a Woman Facing the Law experiences physical and psychological obstacles such that she requires assistance, then the Judge may grant the request of the Woman Facing the Law to have a companion/assistant present.

Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems they face. 34. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services. 35. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among recovery implementers in providing services to recover victims of domestic violence. 36. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 37. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 38. Every person is an individual or corporation. 39. Household means family members, relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION OF VICTIM RECOVERY
Article 60
(1) The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:
a) Health services;
Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing medical treatment and health recovery services to victims.
b) Victim assistance;
Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims.
c) Counseling;
The provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological empowerment of victims.
d) Spiritual guidance;
Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
e) Resocialization.
Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Article 60
(1) The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:
a) Health services;
Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing medical treatment and health recovery services to victims.

Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

ROLE OF THE COMMUNITY
Article 58
(1) The community has the right to obtain the widest possible opportunity to play a role in the protection of women and children.
(2) The role of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities, and mass media.

Article 37
(1) Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 3O is the obligation and responsibility of the government and society.
(2) Special protection for children who are exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various government agencies, companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and society in the elimination of exploitation of children economically and/or sexually.
(3) Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in committing exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

a. life; b. freedom from stigma; c. privacy; d. justice and legal protection; e. education; f. employment, entrepreneurship, and cooperatives; g. health; h. politics; i. religion; j. sports; k. culture and tourism; l. social welfare; m. accessibility; n. Protection of children, not only those who are victims of violence, but also those undergoing judicial processes, as regulated in Law Number 11 of 2012 concerning the Juvenile Justice System, as an improvement to Law Number 3 of 1997 concerning Juvenile Courts, which in Article 3 stipulates that: Every Child in the criminal justice process has the right to:
a. be treated humanely with attention to needs according to their age; b. be separated from adults; c. obtain legal assistance and other assistance effectively; d. engage in recreational activities; e. be free from torture, punishment or other treatment that is cruel, inhumane, and degrading to their dignity and honor; f. not be sentenced to death or life imprisonment; g. not be arrested, detained, or imprisoned, except as a last resort and for the shortest time; h. obtain justice before a Juvenile Court that is objective, impartial, and in a closed session to the public; i. not have their identity published; j. obtain accompaniment from parents/Guardians and persons trusted by the Child; k. obtain social advocacy; l. obtain private life; m. obtain accessibility, especially for disabled children; n. obtain education; From the provisions of the legislation above, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when becoming victims of violence, but in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. In addition, it turns out that the verdicts of District Court judges are still many that are far from the demands of community justice, including families and victims of violence. Hopefully with the enactment of this Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, in Musi Rawas Regency in particular, the handling, and rehabilitation as well as reintegration can be carried out well, and the process of preventing violence against women and children becomes smoother, so that there is less and ultimately no more violence against women and children.
