Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION OF VICTIM RECOVERY
Article 60
(1) The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:
a) Health services;
Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing medical treatment and health recovery services to victims.
b) Victim assistance;
Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims.
c) Counseling;
The provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological empowerment of victims.
d) Spiritual guidance;
Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
e) Resocialization.
Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 38
(1) Special protection for children who become victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (napza) as referred to in Article 30, and are involved in their production and distribution, shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the government and society.
(2) Every person is prohibited from deliberately placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of children in the abuse, production and distribution of napza as referred to in paragraph (1).

Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. IMPLEMENTATION OF VICTIM RECOVERY
Article 60
(1) The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:
a) Health services;
Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing medical treatment and health recovery services to victims.
b) Victim assistance;
Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims.
c) Counseling;
The provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological empowerment of victims.
d) Spiritual guidance;
Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
e) Resocialization.
Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

b) Victim assistance;

Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

GENERAL
I. The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as regulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and the entire territory of Indonesia, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on: (a) independence, (b) eternal peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the teachings of trias politica, there are three State powers namely executive power for the administration of government, legislative power as the formulator of laws and regulations and judicial power as the implementer of laws and regulations. In Indonesia, these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of clean and authoritative government, from the national level to the regional level.
The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of Power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.
The Rights of Women and Children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.
Regional Autonomy that is implemented, has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (Regional Regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to become a guideline for Regional Governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.
This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children, is based on Pancasila, and the 1945 Constitution, and refers to Laws that regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence, among which are Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 Year 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 29 Year 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 11 Year 2012 concerning Juvenile Justice, Law Number 17 Year 2016 concerning Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 Year 2016 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection into Law, and other related Laws, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities, Supreme Court Regulation Number 3 Year 2017 concerning Guidelines for Adjudicating Cases of Women in Conflict with the Law, The principles of this Perda are principles contained in previous laws and regulations, for example the principle of respect for Human Rights and gender equality and justice, are actually already contained in

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Kabupaten is Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 2. Kabupaten Government is the Government of Kabupaten Musi Rawas; 3. Bupati is the Bupati of Musi Rawas. 4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Article 57
The judge on their own initiative or upon request of the parties, public prosecutor, legal counsel and/or victim may order a Woman in Contact with the Law to have her testimony heard through examination via remote audio visual communication at the local court or at another location, if:

2) Based on the judge's assessment, the safety of the Woman in Contact with the Law cannot be guaranteed if she is in a public and open place; or
3) Based on the decision of the Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK), the Woman in Contact with the Law is declared to be in a witness and/or victim protection program and, according to LPSK, cannot attend the trial to give testimony either due to security reasons or due to obstacles, or due to physical and psychological obstacles.

Article 28H paragraph (2), which essentially regulates the rights of citizens to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equality and justice, naturally including women and children victims of violence.
Violence with victims being women and children occurs both within marriage and outside marriage. Whereas Law Number 1 Year 1974 concerning Marriage, which in Article 1 regulates the definition of marriage as a physical and spiritual bond between a man and a woman to build a household based on the One Supreme God. Article 30 stipulates that the obligations of husband and wife are to be mutually faithful, loving, and helpful.
In this Marriage Law, provisions are made regarding who constitutes biological children, as well as joint assets, including the manner of continuing their ownership or inheritance to the children. If this Law is complied with, it can prevent and eliminate Domestic Violence; unfortunately, what occurs in society is that Domestic Violence (KDRT) is increasingly rampant, precisely with modus operandi that are increasingly complex and cause increasingly horrifying consequences. The principle of non-discrimination is in line with the recognition of Human Rights, therefore it is very appropriate that the Government of Indonesia, by enacting Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), in Article 1 states the definition of discrimination against women and all its consequences if discrimination against women occurs.
Basically, working is only for adults, whereas children, namely persons under 18 years of age, have the obligation to pursue education and play. However, due to family economic limitations, there are some children who must work. Therefore Law Number 20 Year 1999 concerning Minimum Age Limit for Children to be able to work provides provisions that parents and employers should pay attention to the provisions of this Law, so that even though children are forced to work, they do not lose their youth and can still attend school to secure their future. Children who are forced to work are found in all areas, both in urban and rural areas. In order for children to obtain their rights, socialization of Law Number 20 Year 1999 is urgent to be carried out.
As a consequence of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as a State that participated in signing the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights becomes the answer. Considering that although since Indonesia's Independence, the 1945 Constitution also stated recognition of Human Rights as regulated in Articles 27 to 34, in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence which clearly constitutes a violation of Human Rights. In Law Number 39 Year 1999 it is reaffirmed that women's rights are Human Rights (Article 45) and Article 52 paragraph (2), which states that Children's rights are Human Rights and for the benefit of children's rights they are recognized and protected by law even from the womb.
This means that children are recognized as having freedom and liberty in accordance with their dignity and worth as human beings, so that any form of violence whatsoever must not occur to children, because it constitutes a violation of Human Rights.
The commitment and political will of the Government of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia to protect children is reinforced by the enactment of Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 Year 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

a. be treated humanely with attention to needs according to their age; b. be separated from adults; c. obtain legal assistance and other assistance effectively; d. engage in recreational activities; e. be free from torture, punishment or other treatment that is cruel, inhumane, and degrading to their dignity and honor; f. not be sentenced to death or life imprisonment; g. not be arrested, detained, or imprisoned, except as a last resort and for the shortest time; h. obtain justice before a Juvenile Court that is objective, impartial, and in a closed session to the public; i. not have their identity published; j. obtain accompaniment from parents/Guardians and persons trusted by the Child; k. obtain social advocacy; l. obtain private life; m. obtain accessibility, especially for disabled children; n. obtain education; From the provisions of the legislation above, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when becoming victims of violence, but in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Child is a person under 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 15. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 33.

ROLE OF THE COMMUNITY
Article 58
(1) The community has the right to obtain the widest possible opportunity to play a role in the protection of women and children.
(2) The role of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities, and mass media.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION OF VICTIM RECOVERY
Article 60
(1) The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:
a) Health services;
Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing medical treatment and health recovery services to victims.
b) Victim assistance;
Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims.
c) Counseling;
The provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological empowerment of victims.
d) Spiritual guidance;
Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
e) Resocialization.
Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 4O
Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 30 includes: physical, psychological, and sexual violence carried out through efforts: dissemination and socialization of statutory provisions that protect child victims of criminal acts of violence; and monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.
Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, (2) ordering to commit, or participating in committing violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties. 14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairments so as to disrupt their growth and development normally. 20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster child is a child cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's normal growth and development. 23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests. 24. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government, and the state. 25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect. 28. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred. 29. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically. 30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence. 31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Article 83 states: Every person who traffics, sells, or kidnaps a child for themselves or to be sold, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 3 (three) years and a fine of at most Rp. 300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and at least Rp. 60,000,000,- (sixty million rupiah). These three Articles are very reformative Articles when compared with the provisions in the Criminal Code, which in articles 281 to 296 regulate provisions, where the heaviest criminal threat is Article 295, namely 12 years. When compared, the Child Protection Law has been quite severe in establishing criminal threats and fines as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83. The problem is, even though the Law has established heavy threats or legal sanctions, there are still Law Enforcement Officials who have not optimally implemented them, so there is still a long way to go, between law in book and law in action. In cases as regulated in Article 81 to Article 83, Law Officials often conduct investigation and inquiry processes that are quite heavy and exhausting for child victims of violence, but in prosecution and judges' verdicts they are still light so they are not in accordance with justice. Violence against women and children also occurs frequently within the household scope, even though we have had a law for 13 years, namely Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (KDRT), but nowadays domestic violence is increasing in number. For the prevention and handling of domestic violence in Musi Rawas Regency, the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Musi Rawas Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency, based on the Decree of the Regent of Musi Rawas Number 703/KPTS/KPP/2015, namely concerning the Establishment of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) of Musi Rawas Regency. The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) serves as a place for reporting, handling, rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of violence. If there is domestic violence or other violence affecting women and children, it must be reported to the P2TP2A, however the existence of P2TP2A is not yet widely known by the community. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, in essence is to realize a household that is sakinah, mawadah, and warohmah, this can be read from the objectives of eliminating domestic violence, namely: (a) preventing all forms of domestic violence (KDRT); (b) protecting victims of domestic violence, (c) taking action against perpetrators of domestic violence and (d) maintaining the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household. So that we better understand the prohibition of domestic violence, the important matters from Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning domestic violence will be briefly described as follows: Types of domestic violence, include:
a. physical violence, is an act that results in (1) pain, (2) falling ill, or (3) serious injury; b. psychological violence, is an act that results in (1) fear, (2) loss of self-confidence, (3) loss of ability to act, (4) feeling of helplessness, (5) and/or severe psychological suffering to a person; c. sexual violence includes: (1) forced sexual relations committed against a person including a child, who resides within the household scope, (2) forced sexual relations against one person within their household scope with another person including a child, for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes; d. household neglect, includes (1) neglecting a person including a child within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person or child, (2) resulting in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. The rights of domestic violence victims are to obtain: (1) protection from family, police, prosecutor's office, court, advocates, social institutions, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order; (2) health services in accordance with medical needs; (3) special handling related to victim confidentiality; (4) accompaniment by social workers and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and (5) spiritual guidance services. All parties both from government elements, Law Enforcement Officials (APH) and NGOs, have become members of the P2TP2A of Musi Rawas Regency. The obligation to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is in sync with the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. In this Law it is stipulated that the authority to carry out women's empowerment and child protection is handed over to Regional Governments, so it is a very good opportunity for Regional Governments including the Regional Government of Musi Rawas Regency, nowadays to establish Regional Regulations with a gender equality and justice perspective and children's rights. This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, is established in accordance with the provisions of Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning the Formation of Legislation. The material of this Law provides complete guidance regarding the formal juridical and material juridical requirements that must be met if we want to establish legislation, including Regional Regulations, starting from the preparation of Academic Papers (NA), to Draft Regency/City Regional Regulations.

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the domestic sphere. 5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is the guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. 6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 8. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim. 9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 12.
